_what: Take selection for the recording of 2026-10-06. The recording is 321s and contains retakes, revised lines and cut lines. This file records WHICH audio was kept and why, so the edit is reproducible and reviewable. Source: inputs/vo_raw.m4a, unmodified.
_rule: Last complete take wins, which is the convention the recording script asks for ('say the line again and carry on'). Every cut point was placed at a measured silence trough (10ms RMS), not at a recogniser word boundary, because several joins are butt-ended in the word timings.

segments.says: Rutherford Chang began CENTS with a simple value discrepancy. What was one cent to the US Treasury was about two and a half cents as copper at the time he made the piece. Nothing had been sold for a single cent since before Chang was born,
yet the object remained, buoyed into physicality by the force of its context.
The readymade he chose is also perhaps the most reproduced physical artwork on Earth.
More than 500 billion Lincoln cents were produced, each with the portrait of Lincoln that Victor David Brenner made in 1909.
It is absurd that a nation's currency should dissolve into worthlessness.
It is absurd that a cent should be valued at hundreds or thousands of dollars. Yet here we are.
segments.takes: only complete take; a false start 'It is absurd.' at 66.58 is dropped

segments.says: Chang brings a kind of black hole humor to his work,
laughing at this absurdity with a laughter that resonates within emptiness.
segments.takes: same take as G1, continued. The 2.00s the speaker left mid-sentence is cut to 0.46s: it is one sentence, and two seconds reads as a full stop.

segments.says: In the system Chang created, every cent is passed through five transformations of value. One, in circulation... Two... Three... Four, destroyed, melted into a block of copper, its value made undefinable.
segments.takes: revised version; the earlier 'Every cent passes through five transformations of value' at 117.92 and a false start at 125.40 are dropped

segments.says: Five, inscribed on Bitcoin, its value continually redefined by decentralized consensus as the objects are traded every day on the open market.
segments.takes: LAST of ~12 attempts spanning 165.2-288.9; this is the only one that reaches 'on the open market'. A stray 'it.' at 288.84 is excluded.

segments.says: Chang cracks open the worthless one-cent coin and allows it to function as a vessel of indeterminate value and emergent meaning.
segments.takes: only take, clean. 0.45s of silence is prepended because the recording starts 0.07s before the first word and a butt join needs air.

segments.says: CENTS is a becoming, a gesture that unfolds continually through the actions of its participants through time.
segments.takes: 3rd of 3; earlier at 291.58 and 303.80. Note: 'through time', not the essay's 'in time'.

_gap_note: Segment G was one span until 2026-10-06. The speaker left 2.00s of silence between 'to his work,' and 'laughing', which reads as a sentence break in a sentence that has none. Split and rejoined with 0.46s. Whisper's word timings put the gap at 1.34s; the measured energy says 2.00s, and the energy is what was cut on.
_multi_source: A second recording was made 2026-10-08 for the line before the closer. Segments declare their source. The new take measured 3.25 dB hotter than the main one at matched gating, so it carries a gain: loudnorm normalises the WHOLE file, so a level difference between sources survives it and the line would sit proud of the film.
